citation: Unknown author(s) (2023). Assessing the Viability of Laser-Activated Dental Bleaching Compared to Conventional In-Office Bleaching Methods. Applied Sciences.
source_type: systematic review (19 clinical trials, 20 in vitro studies)
laser_device: UNKNOWN (unspecified laser types used for bleaching activation across included studies)
hazard_studied: postoperative tooth sensitivity and hard tissue (enamel/dentin) alterations associated with laser-activated bleaching
parameter_or_operator_factor: gel contact time and hydrogen peroxide concentration (laser activation reduced contact time and HP concentration needed); no laser power/speed parameters stated
adverse_outcome: review found no significant differences in sensitivity or hard tissue alterations between laser-activated and conventional (non-activated) bleaching groups
relevance_to_project: Tangential to an ex-vivo diode-laser oral soft-tissue study since this concerns hard-tissue (enamel/dentin) bleaching safety rather than soft-tissue surgery, but it is dental-laser adverse-outcome literature relevant to the broader safety review.

citation: Unknown author(s) (2026). Comparative bubble dynamics of plasma-mediated Nd:YAG laser-induced optical breakdown and thermally driven Er:YAG laser-activated irrigation in water. Lasers in Medical Science.
laser_device: 1064 nm Nd:YAG (plasma-mediated LIOB) and 2940 nm Er:YAG (laser-activated irrigation, LAI)
hazard_studied: physical bubble dynamics (size, lifetime, expansion rate, rebound) produced by different laser pulse energies during root-canal laser-activated irrigation; a mechanical/thermal energy-delivery characterization, not a direct tissue-injury endpoint
parameter_or_operator_factor: pulse energy (LIOB: 100/200/300 mJ per pulse; LAI: 10/15/20 mJ per pulse)
adverse_outcome: UNKNOWN — study reports differences in bubble size/expansion/rebound by energy setting; it does not report tissue damage, extrusion injury, or clinical adverse events
causality_established: DIRECT_EVIDENCE (for the pulse-energy-to-bubble-dynamics relationship only; no tissue-damage causal claim is made or should be inferred)
relevance_to_project: Only loosely relevant to an ex-vivo diode-laser oral soft-tissue study since it uses different laser types (Nd:YAG/Er:YAG) and a root-canal/hard-tissue irrigation context, but it shares the methodological theme of how delivered pulse-energy parameters produce measurable, energy-dependent physical effects relevant to output verification.
